doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Leonard Heywood, his mentor
summary: Leonard Heywood was his first drum teacher, band director and mentor; he left for Arizona and Purdie wants to dedicate his book to him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Who were the teachers that you would credit?
Well my biggest teacher was Leonard Heywood. That was my first teacher and he was my music teacher, my drum teacher, he was the band director for the school, and my mentor.

Heywood. Leonard Heywood. When I lost him, he moved to — well his wife said — moved to Phoenix, Arizona, for his health. Well I have no idea if that was true or not. As far as I’m concerned it was. Because she said it. But as time and the years go by it makes you wonder. Did they split up? He was an alcoholic, but of course I didn’t know what that was. They said he had a breathing problem. Okay, Arizona was the dry place. I mean I had the whole spiel. It was all given to me. And I believed it. Totally believed it. I had never thought anything different. I had no reason to think that anything was different until 20, 30 years later, when you start asking and asking and then the things change on you. Well I just started hearing all kinds of stories. But who knows why? I was not that inquisitive to that point to want to know why they broke up, why they separated, why they divorced, whatever they did. I still have no idea. He was my mentor, he was my teacher, I loved him, and what I wanted to do was dedicate my book, my first book, and © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
anything else that I could do over the course of the years, to him. Because of what he did for me.
And still it will happen, and I’ll just keep on doing it.
